messages.content: "Imagine you are planning a vacation to Paris, France. You want to stay at the 'Hotel Le Bristol Paris' in a suite room for 10 days starting from 12-01-2022. You also have a preference for a city view from your room. How would you book this hotel? After booking, you want to know how much 1000 US dollars would be in Euros. Can you find out the latest exchange rate? On your way to the hotel, you want to stop by a Safeway store in Palo Alto, CA to pick up some items. You need to order 2 bottles of water, 3 apples, and 1 loaf of bread. How would you place this order? Lastly, you are curious about the universe and want to know how long it would take for light to travel from Earth to Proxima Centauri, which is approximately 4.24 light years away, considering the speed of light in vacuum is 299792458 m/s. Can you calculate this?"

function.name: book_hotel
function.description: Book a room in a specific hotel with particular preferences Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_date.description: The starting date of the stay in format MM-DD-YYYY.

stay_duration.description: The duration of the stay in days.

view.description: The preferred view from the room, can be ignored if no preference. If none provided, assumes no preference.

function.name: safeway_order
function.description: Order specified items from a Safeway location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location of the Safeway store, e.g. Palo Alto, CA.

quantity.description: Quantity of each item in the order list.

function.name: latest_exchange_rate
function.description: Retrieve the latest exchange rate between two specified currencies. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

source_currency.description: The currency you are converting from.

target_currency.description: The currency you are converting to.

amount.description: The amount to be converted. If omitted, default to xchange rate of 1 unit source currency.

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years. This is a float type value.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.
